title: Who receives industry research money in San Francisco
question: Which San Francisco hospitals and institutions receive the most research money from drug and device makers?
finding: Manufacturers reported $923.1 million in research payments to 593 San Francisco recipients for 2019 to 2025. 48% of it, $441.0 million, is recorded under one name, Langley Porter Psychiatric Hospital, although only 0.4% of those dollars are on studies whose lead investigator is listed under psychiatry; the largest single field is Internal Medicine, 14%. The manufacturers' label for the recipient looks wrong rather than the conduct. Next are UCSF Medical Center ($85.2 million), University of California San Francisco ($79.7 million), Board of Trustees of the Leland Stanford Junior University ($55.1 million). Research payments are disclosed.
how: Research-payment records in the federal Open Payments files whose recipient has a San Francisco address, added up by recipient name for 2019 to 2025. Spellings that differ only by punctuation, spacing or the word "the" are merged; names that are really different are left apart, so one university can appear on several rows. The top field is the specialty most often listed for the lead investigators on a recipient's payments, weighted by dollars.
limits: Research payments are disclosed. In these records 98.8% of the money names a hospital or other institution as the recipient, not a physician. The manufacturer chooses how to name the recipient, which is why one institution can appear under several names and why a psychiatric teaching hospital heads the list. The file holds only what manufacturers reported, and it has a column marking payments whose publication was delayed, so recent years can rise later.
